newsitem.title: USA: American Air pilots board recesses talks.
newsitem.headline: American Air pilots board recesses talks.

text.p: The American Airlines pilots union said on Thursday its board recessed meetings without taking a vote on a labor contract proposed by the carrier.
Meetings will resume Friday, a spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association told reporters.
"There should be a vote sometime tomorrow," said Wally Pitts, spokesman for APA, which represents 9,300 American Airlines pilots.
American Airlines is a subsidiary of AMR Corp.
"The board wants to be fresh for what's expected to be a long debate tomorrow," said Brian Mayhew, chairman of the negotiating committee for the APA board.
"I can't imagine there won't be a vote tomorrow," Mayhew told reporters. "They owe it to the membership to vote one way or another tomorrow."
Pitts had said the issue of who will fly smaller jets at American Airlines' regional carrier, American Eagle, remained at the center of the meeting this afternoon.
American Airlines pilots are concerned they might lose routes to American Eagle if American Airlines buys new smaller jets for the regional subsidiary.

"The members today are trying to educate themselves on the small jet issue and that takes time," Pitts told a news conference earlier Thursday in the Chicago suburb of Arlington Heights where the meetings are being held.
